description: Search video by what it shows. Each clip is indexed as keyframes embedded with Amazon Nova; a text query finds the nearest frames. A CDL keyframe-search demo.

about.title: About this demo
body: This is the CDL public interface, searching video instead of still images. Each video clip is sampled into keyframes; every frame is embedded with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings (3072-d) and indexed with pgvector. A text query is embedded the same way and matched to the nearest frames, then results collapse to the parent clip.

The corpus is ~105 public MSR-VTT video clips plus 300 COCO images, loaded into a personal CDL dev stage. Offline, this keyframe approach reached recall@10 of 79% on the 1,000-clip MSR-VTT benchmark — competitive with trained video-retrieval models.

sections.heading: How to read a result
body: Green ‘image’ means the clip matched by its visual content (the vector search), not by keywords. Click a result to see the clip's frames.
